subject: Follow-up & shortlist: model slate for Orion pilot (cost / latency tradeoffs)
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel@orion.ai>
Cc: procurement@orion.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & shortlist: model slate for Orion pilot (cost / latency tradeoffs)

Hi all — thanks again for the demo call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed next step list so we keep momentum: 

1) Shortlist (first-pass, ranked by fit -> ops):
   - Option A: redwood/gpt-compat-13b-q4 (strong quality, mid latency, best on hallucination tests)
   - Option B: open/xlm-lite-14b-int8 (low cost, slightly higher latency at peak)
   - Option C: redwood/compact-8b-rt (lowest latency, some quality drop on long-context Q/A)

2) Why these three: matched to your real-time classifying + summarization flow; A is safest on long-form summaries, B gives best cost-per-request, C is the path if sub-100ms tail latency matters for UX. See attached benchmark CSV and the prompt examples used for scoring.

3) Open items from the call:
   - Daniel: confirm target p95 latency (you mentioned ~250ms for single-turn assistant)
   - Procurement: timeline for PO / SOW (we flagged a pilot budget in the ~$30k–50k range)
   - Ops: Marissa, confirm whether Orion requires on-prem/private deployment or VPC-only (I noted compliance constraints)

Proposed next steps (simple mutual action plan):
   a) We run a 48-hour targeted benchmark across the three candidates with your prompt set (we can include a quantized variant of A).
   b) You supply a small labeled sample (50–100 items) for quality-regression monitoring.
   c) We share a short MAP doc and procurement checklist by end of the week.

Attachments: benchmarking CSV (benchmarks used), prompt examples (.jsonl), and a one-page MAP draft.

If that sounds good, Ben and Marissa — can you own the benchmark run and the ops checklist respectively? Daniel, if you can confirm the latency target and share the labeled sample by Friday that would be perfect.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.n@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel@orion.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & shortlist: model slate for Orion pilot (cost / latency tradeoffs)

Thanks Priya — happy to run the benchmark. Quick notes from my side after looking through the CSV:

- Benchmarks were run at sequence lengths of 128 / 512; for Orion’s summarization use-case we should bias toward 512 for tail behavior. I’ll re-run with 512 and with more realistic concurrency (50–100 qps) to capture batching effects.
- Preliminary cost delta (token-unit equivalent): A ~1.8x cost vs C, B ~1.2x vs C. Will add per-100k request estimates on the rerun.
- Quality: A wins consistently on hallucination and instruction-following. B has occasional truncation on long bullet lists we tested; C misses finer entity extraction cases.

Question for Daniel: when you say "single-turn assistant p95 250ms", is that measured cold-start or warm (cache)? Our target would be warm p95 — cold starts vary by model size.

Action: I’ll kick the rerun today and upload results to the Drive link Priya included. ETA: 48 hours.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.c@redwood.com

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick clarifications from Orion: 

- Latency target: 250ms p95 warm is correct for the MVP UX. Cold start acceptable up to 1s for occasional autoscale events.
- Deployment: VPC-hosted Redwood Dedicated would be ideal; we only need on-prem if a later security review flags it.
- Labeled sample: I can share 75 labeled entries (intent + golden summary) by EOD Friday.
- Budget: procurement@orion.ai will follow-up on PO timing; target to close pilot PO in the next 2–3 weeks.

Two asks: 
1) Can you include a head-to-head latency vs cost scatter for the three candidates (warm p50/p95/p99) on the rerun?
2) For quality regression: can Redwood produce a lightweight smoke test harness that runs daily and alerts for regression deltas > 3% on ROUGE/EM metrics?

If you can confirm those, we’ll prioritize moving to the pilot.

—Daniel
Daniel Cho

Looping in a quick ops checklist and one operational note: 

Ops checklist (Marissa, Redwood):
- Confirm VPC peering window and required IP ranges — target 2 business days to provision once PO is received.
- Autoscale policy: configure conservative ramp for first week (max burst 2x baseline).
- Logging & audit: enable token-level trace for pilot (retention 30 days).
- Regression harness: I can deliver a lightweight daily runner (Python script + small dataset) and wire up alerts to your Slack. Needs the sample Daniel promised.

Operational note: if Orion expects sustained peaks > 70 qps we should consider Option B as default for the pilot and run A in canary for quality verification. Option C remains the low-latency fallback but may require guardrails for hallucination-prone prompts.

I’ll attach a one-page ops MAP and timeline to the Drive link once Ben’s rerun completes.

Marissa
